title: Cashiering Application Rule for Electric Service by Rate Schedule: Energy Assistance Agency Payments and the Current Bill
content:
**Rule.** In figuring the late-charged amount of the most recent Electric Service by Rate Schedule bill, the payments of the month — payments dated less than one whole month before the current date — reach the bill as follows. "Agency payments" are the payments of the month through the energy assistance agency channel; "the agency" is the agency of those payments (where they come from more than one agency, the agency of the latest of them). The "earlier unpaid balance" is what the account owed before the month: the current account balance less the usage lines, program charge lines, late payment charges and fees dated in the month, plus the payments and bill credits dated in the month, less the returned payments dated in the month, never less than zero.

| Situation in the month | Payments that reach the bill |
|---|---|
| Agency payments exist and the agency has no pledge recorded on the account in the month | All the agency payments, applied to this bill directly, together with the part of the other payments of the month that exceeds the earlier unpaid balance (never less than zero) |
| Agency payments exist and the agency has a pledge recorded on the account in the month | Only the part of the other payments of the month that exceeds the earlier unpaid balance (never less than zero); the agency payments are left to that pledge |
| No agency payment in the month | The part of all payments of the month that exceeds the earlier unpaid balance (never less than zero), payments being applied to the oldest charges first |

### Training questions answered by the rule

**An agency pays $90.00 with no pledge on file this month, and the member also paid $200.00. The earlier unpaid balance is $250.00. What reaches the bill?** The $90.00 agency payment in full; the member's $200.00 does not exceed $250.00, so none of it reaches the bill. $90.00 reaches the bill.

**Same facts, but the agency recorded a pledge on the account this month.** The $90.00 is left to the pledge; the member's $200.00 does not exceed $250.00. Nothing reaches the bill.

**No agency payment; the member paid $290.00; earlier unpaid balance $250.00.** $40.00 reaches the bill.

**Does a pledge recorded by a different agency than the paying agency change the first answer?** No. What matters is whether the paying agency has a pledge recorded on the account in the month.
